conflicts.issue: Step 5 must run in a maintenance window, but one constraint specifies maintenance and another restricts it to business-hours Mon-Thu only with no incidents; these can conflict with the product quiet-period timing.
Step 5 requires a maintenance window and quiet period, while ProductPM requires no launch window or major event and customer notice 14 days before the drop; timing may block the drop window.

SRE requires a safe maintenance window and stable post-cutover error rate before destructive drop, while ProductPM requires support readiness and avoidance of launch/major-event windows; these jointly constrain when the drop can occur.

Security requires explicit cascade review and approval before merge, while ConsumerSubsystem requires a cutover test proving the generated drop SQL is non-destructive; both must be satisfied and may surface conflicting outcomes if the cascade is dangerous.

BackendOwner wants join-table reads/writes before dropping assignee_id, while ConsumerSubsystem requires old assignee_id write shim until all writers are updated; these align on a transition window but still impose a dependency that delays read-switch cutover until writer parity.

BackendOwner wants read-switch after backfill and dual-write verification, while DataPlatform requires bounded backfill batches and the join table fully created before read switch; this is compatible but strictly serializes deployment.
